scope.note: No numbered R or C identifier falls in this scope, so every requirement is an S requirement and all 27 base units are newly accounted.

independent_review.why_this_scope_is_high_risk: This is where the standard's processor latitude lives. A permission wrongly promoted to a requirement, or a plan inferring behaviour from evaluation order, would corrupt every later expression fixture.

evaluation_freedoms.freedom: side effects in IF, WHERE and FORALL contexts
pure elemental operations may be performed in any order or simultaneously
evaluation may be skipped for a conditional expression

table_10_2_assessment.detail: The enumeration-type and character-kind distinctions are preserved. Automatic extraction interleaves table columns, so the reviewer checked the treatment against the table itself rather than accepting the candidate's summary.

oracle_discipline_verified: No plan infers anything from which operand was evaluated, in what order, or whether it was evaluated at all.
No plan asserts a result that a mathematically equivalent rewrite could change, and no floating-point tolerance is used as an escape hatch.
Grouping of an associative intrinsic operation is not claimed to be value-observable; the defined-extension route remains owned by 10.1.6 and 15.4.3.4.2.
No compiler agreement, address arithmetic, TRANSFER, emitted assembly or undefined read is used as an oracle.
explicit_limitations: Source registration only: no test program, compiler invocation, oracle, canonical link, SourceUse relationship or fixture approval is created.
All 91 facets remain pending. Several are bounded by processor latitude and record what may not be asserted rather than a program that could be written today.
The expression grammar remains owned by the registered 10.1.2 catalogues, intrinsic assignment by 10.2.1.3, defined operations by 15.4.3.4.x, and 10.1.6 through 10.1.12 remain dependencies.
Clause 10 remains partially registered: 10.1.5.2 onwards and most of 10.2 are unauthored.
